NC-2025E1-HB3.policyArea: AGRICULTURE; AGRICULTURE DEPT.; APPROPRIATIONS; BUDGETING; DEBTOR & CREDITOR; FINES & PENALTIES; FUELS; FUNDS & ACCOUNTS; NOTIFICATION; PRESENTED; PUBLIC; PUBLIC OFFICIALS; RATIFIED; REVENUE DEPT.; STATE CONTROLLER; TAXATION; TAXES, FUEL; CHAPTERED; TAX COLLECTION
NC-2025E1-HB3.aiSummary: North Carolina law suspends the motor fuel tax from the day after it became law through November 30, 2026, setting the tax rate at zero cents per gallon. It also moves money from a state reserve to help replace funds that would have gone to road, water, wildlife, and cleanup accounts. Through December 31, 2026, it bars civil and criminal penalties for dyed diesel used for farming and related work, and it gives certain farmers, loggers, fishermen, and wildlife managers a tax break on dyed diesel used in highway vehicles.

NC-2025-HB1246.aiSummary: The bill would add rules against using troops or armed people at voting places near Election Day, with some exceptions for law enforcement and emergency help. It would also make voter threats, coercion, and certain false voter challenges crimes, create money for voter education, and let people seek court orders and damages if they are targeted. The bill would also protect election workers from threats, change early voting hours for all county sites, and start those early voting changes on January 1, 2027. The visible text also begins a new section on election certification, but no new rule is shown yet.

NC-2025-HB920.aiSummary: North Carolina enacted a law that sets rules for virtual currency kiosks, which are automated machines used to move money into virtual currency. It requires kiosk operators to give clear warnings about risks, fees, exchange rates, scams, and customer liability before and during transactions, and it lets the state banking commissioner review records and enforce the rules. The law also bans login by QR code or similar scan-based methods and limits access to manual entry methods.

NC-2025-SB1076.aiSummary: The law limits how Rocky Mount and Louisburg can move money from their electric utility revenues, and it also limits how Rocky Mount can use natural gas utility revenue. It sets up a Rocky Mount Public Utilities Advisory Committee to review utility rates, budgets, major contracts, service policies, and fund transfers, but the committee can only advise the city. The natural gas and utility revenue limits for Rocky Mount are effective when the law takes effect; the Rocky Mount natural gas part ends on January 1, 2029.

NC-2025-SB675.aiSummary: The bill would set rules for charitable groups that are named as beneficiaries of some non-will property transfers, like payable-on-death accounts, insurance, retirement plans, and similar assets. It would let a charity ask for the property or related info with a sworn affidavit and set what papers must be shown, while limiting what personal information the holder of the property can ask for from the charity’s staff or board. It also gives a process and time limits for delivery, court action, and payments back to a donor’s estate if needed. The act would take effect when it becomes law and apply to affidavits delivered on or after that date.
